procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit on his lunch break from the break room at work. Overdue 6-month BP check was rescheduled twice for shifts, so doing it by video.

He bought a cuff at the pharmacy in January, readings mostly 128-136 over 78-84 mornings. Taking lisinopril daily. No headaches or lightheadedness. Back and knees about the same; neck fine.

A/P: HTN controlled by home readings, continue lisinopril 10. Next in-person at the September physical with labs. Send me readings through the portal if they run over 140.

documents.title: neck and arm
documents.author: patient
documents.body: my neck has been killing me for about 10 days and now it goes down my left arm. thumb and pointer finger feel numb half the time. didnt hurt it that i know of. can i get in next week

documents.title: RE: neck and arm
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sorry to hear it. Any weakness where you're dropping things, trouble walking, or trouble with bladder or bowels? If yes, go to the ED. Otherwise I've put you in Monday at 7:40 with the doctor.

events.reason: Neck pain radiating to left arm

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: left arm radicular symptoms with weakness

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About 2 weeks of left-sided neck pain, now running into the left arm, with numbness of the thumb and index finger that comes and goes. No injury he can name, but 30-odd years of lifting. Ibuprofen takes the edge off; cyclobenzaprine helps him sleep. No gait trouble, no bowel or bladder change, right arm fine. Pain 6/10.

O: BP as charted. Neck: limited extension, left paraspinal tenderness. Left wrist extension slightly weak, 4+/5; grip and the rest of the arm full strength. Light touch reduced over the left thumb and index finger. Reflexes symmetric to my exam. Right arm normal. Gait normal.

A/P: Left cervical radicular symptoms on known C5-C7 spondylosis, with a mild motor finding. MRI C-spine ordered and PM&R referral placed. Continue ibuprofen and cyclobenzaprine as needed, no overhead lifting for now. Return or ED for spreading weakness, gait change, bladder or bowel symptoms.

reports.text:
MRI CERVICAL SPINE WITHOUT CONTRAST
Indication: left neck and arm pain with thumb and index numbness.
Technique: multiplanar multisequence imaging without contrast.
Comparison: none.
Findings: Alignment maintained. Vertebral body heights preserved; no fracture or marrow lesion. Cord normal in caliber and signal. Craniocervical junction normal.
C2-C3 through C4-C5: no significant disc bulge or stenosis.
C5-C6: disc desiccation and disc height loss with a broad degenerative bulge; canal and foramina adequate, no root compression.
C6-C7: disc desiccation and height loss. Left-sided disc herniation compresses the exiting left nerve root. No cord compression. Right foramen patent.
C7-T1: unremarkable.
Paraspinal soft tissues normal.
reports.conclusion:
1. Multilevel degenerative disc disease at C5-C6 and C6-C7.
2. Left-sided C6-C7 disc herniation with compression of the left exiting nerve root.
3. No cord compression.

documents.title: MRI result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Douglas, the MRI shows a disc bulging out at C6-C7 on the left and pressing on the nerve root there, on top of the wear-and-tear changes you already knew about. The spinal cord itself is fine. That fits your arm symptoms. You're on the books with PM&R next Wednesday and they'll go over treatment. Keep avoiding overhead lifting until then.

documents.title: RE: MRI result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ok thanks. my brother had surgery for this, hoping i dont need that

documents.title: RE: MRI result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Most people with this improve without surgery, usually with therapy and time. Let's see what PM&R thinks.

documents.title: Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation Consultation
documents.author: physiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PHYSICAL MEDICINE & REHABILITATION CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 07/03/2024
Reason for referral: neck pain with left arm symptoms.

History: 55-year-old warehouse loader with four weeks of neck pain that has steadily worsened and now travels into the left arm, with numbness in the thumb and index finger. He recalls no injury. Long history of heavy manual work. Known cervical spondylosis with disc degeneration at C5-C6 and C6-C7. Hypertension. Mechanical low back pain after L4-L5 laminectomy in 2022. Osteoarthritis of both knees. Left rotator cuff repair 2016.

Medications: lisinopril 10 mg daily; ibuprofen 600 mg TID PRN; cyclobenzaprine 5 mg QHS PRN; acetaminophen 500 mg PRN.
Allergies: sulfa (urticaria); shellfish (reaction unknown).
Family history: father with cervical spondylosis and myelopathy, hypertension; mother with osteoarthritis and osteoporosis; older brother with cervical radiculopathy treated with ACDF.
Social: former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 5 years ago; 1-2 beers on weekends.

Examination: Alert, comfortable seated. Weakness of the left biceps and left wrist extensors. Sensation reduced over the lateral left forearm and the thumb and index finger. Left brachioradialis reflex diminished; other upper limb reflexes symmetric. Right arm normal. No Hoffmann sign, gait steady.

Imaging: MRI of the cervical spine 6/26/2024 reviewed: C6-C7 disc herniation with nerve root compression, on multilevel degenerative disc disease.

Impression: Left cervical radiculopathy, on a background of multilevel cervical spondylosis.

Plan:
- Physical therapy for cervical traction, mobility and scapular strengthening; referral sent.
- Continue ibuprofen and cyclobenzaprine as needed.
- Avoid heavy overhead lifting for the time being.
- Follow up here in 6 to 8 weeks.

Thank you for the referral.
Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation

documents.title: Physical Therapy Initial Evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
PHYSICAL THERAPY INITIAL EVALUATION, 7/10/2024
Dx: left cervical radiculopathy.
Subjective: neck pain into the left arm, thumb and index numb intermittently, worse end of shift.
Objective: cervical extension and left rotation limited. Left wrist extension 4/5, elbow flexion 4/5. Reduced light touch left thumb and index.
Assessment: good rehab candidate.
Plan: 2x/week for 8 weeks: mechanical traction trial, deep neck flexor and scapular work, nerve glides, lifting mechanics for his job, home program.

documents.title: Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation Follow-up
documents.author: physiatry
documents.body:
PM&R FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 08/21/2024

Seven weeks into therapy he reports the left arm numbness is nearly gone and the neck pain is a background ache. Back to regular duties with better lifting habits.

Exam: left biceps and wrist extensor strength full and symmetric. Sensation intact in the left arm and hand. Reflexes symmetric. Neck motion improved.

Impression: left cervical radiculopathy, largely resolved with conservative care.
Plan: finish the remaining therapy sessions, then the home exercise program. Ibuprofen and cyclobenzaprine as needed. Return as needed if symptoms recur.

documents.title: Physical Therapy Discharge Summary
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
PT DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Visits attended: 15 of 16, 7/10/2024 to 9/4/2024.
Status: arm symptoms resolved, neck pain 1-2/10 at worst. Cervical motion full but end-range stiffness in extension. Left upper extremity strength 5/5 throughout.
Goals met. Discharged to home exercise program.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL, 55M

Interval: left cervical radiculopathy this summer (MRI 6/26, C6-7 herniation on the left), treated by PM&R with PT, finished 9/4. Arm numbness and weakness gone. Does his neck exercises most nights. Back and knees unchanged, ibuprofen on heavy days.
BP fine on his home cuff. PHQ-2 0. No other complaints.

Exam: BP as charted. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Neck: mild end-range stiffness, Spurling negative both sides. Arms: strength 5/5, sensation and reflexes symmetric. Knees crepitus, no effusion.

A/P
- Left cervical radiculopathy: resolved. Off the active list.
- Cervical spondylosis/DDD: home program.
- HTN controlled, lisinopril 10.
- LBP and knee OA stable.
- Labs today (CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c). Lung CT November, ordered. Flu and COVID at the pharmacy, he prefers it near home.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Everything from Wednesday came back normal, including the sugar test (A1c) and blood counts. See you in the spring.

documents.title: Outside immunizations
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Registry shows influenza (trivalent) and updated COVID-19 vaccines given 10/12/2024 at a community pharmacy. Added to the record.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST FOR LUNG CANCER SCREENING
Comparison: 11/8/2023 and 11/9/2022.
Findings: Lungs clear. No nodule, mass or consolidation. No emphysema. No effusion. Normal heart size. Mediastinum without adenopathy. Unchanged mild degenerative thoracic spine changes.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1. Negative. Continue annual low-dose CT.

documents.title: Lung CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Third year in a row the screening CT is clear. Good news.
